title: Navigate from a source-authorized Command Incident-linked Case to the existing read-only Investigate Case Timeline
goal: Make already authorized linked Investigate Cases navigable from the single Command Work Queue selected Incident view via a fixed same-origin read-only Case Timeline URL. Reauthorization stays with the destination; no source permissions are conveyed in the link.
invariants: Selected Incident must be Command-readable within current Work Queue page before owner lookups; Shared Object Linking and Investigate owner must independently allow each Case before a navigation target is shown.
Only existing trusted same-origin GET /case-timeline?case_id=... route is used; its host and Case/Timeline/typed-source owners MUST independently authenticate/authorize the destination request.
Never place tenant, environment, principal, permission, token, or return authorization in the URL.
Case ID is safely query-encoded by html/template urlquery before interpolation, never treated as HTML, arbitrary external redirect, JavaScript URL, or a source trust signal.
No new API, IAM adapter, source, mutation, persisted link, Class-2 operation, external integration or claim of automatic exact return.
security_properties: No link when Shared link or Investigate Case is missing/denied; no source lookup for unselected Incident/Task/denied current page.
Source-generated Case ID containing query delimiter, hash or angle brackets cannot inject extra tenant params or HTML code.
Navigating URL is a non-authoritative pointer; destination may refuse or not be mounted, and no source data appears in the URL beyond ID already authorized.

migration.rationale: Additive HTML navigation anchor, existing JSON contract and server authorization unchanged

rollback.strategy: Remove link from selected Incident template; retain all Case and source-owned freshness fields
verification: Previous HTML and JSON behavior restored
No owner or route state changed

inputs: CAP-CMD-106 §9,§11,§17,§21,§25 and CAP-CMD-101 §9,§11,§17; existing source-authorized LinkedCaseOwnerJoin of 106B and freshness of 106C
Canonical read-only Case Timeline existing fixed GET /case-timeline?case_id and its independent Case/Entry/source authorization (CAP-INV-110)
outputs: One clickable same-origin Case Timeline target per existing independently authorized selected Incident Case on the existing HTML route; no new server endpoint.
Go HTTP/HTML regression tests for URL escaping, denied source, unselected/Task, JSON backward compatibility.
acceptance_tests: GET /command/work-queue?selected=Incident:inc-a HTML shows a fixed URL-encoded read-only Investigate navigation link for an independently source-authorized Case.
A hostile Case ID with & or # cannot add extra URL query parameters, leak tenant or change destination origin.
Denied/absent Case, unknown Shared links, Task/unselected Incident never show Case navigation.

The linked Case remains independently authorized at the destination: this module never issues authorization, and the receiving host must mount its existing /case-timeline and recheck Case/Timeline/typed-source permissions.
Existing selected Case JSON projection remains identical; exact SHA passes Go tests/race/vet and mandatory engineering gates.
definition_of_ready: Existing E10-CMD-106C-FRESHNESS IMPLEMENTED; Case link and Investigate owner join exist; first-party destination CaseTimelineHTTPHandler exists as independent route.
OPEN-013 Class-2 create/link/mutate excluded, no real production IAM/host/router guaranteed.
definition_of_done: Read-only selected Case navigation appears as source-owned URL after existing independent auth.
Tests and CI GitHub exact SHA verified; no weaker authorization.
Handoff explicitly notes deployment/router and exact return context not implemented; no production claim.

performance_budget.rationale: At most sixteen links generated from the already authorized selected Incident Case projection; no new provider reads or network calls.
